Tool: built-in image_gen.imagegen; transparent_background=true.
References: approved V1 sprite sheet and original individual frames 00, 04, 05, 06.

RUN AND INITIAL TRANSITION PASS:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production pixel sprite ANIMATION INBETWEENS. The input is our approved 4x4 sheet of ONE specific adult spotted orange deer with golden branching antlers. Preserve this same character design, exact chunky black-outline pixel-art style, warm orange/brown palette, white back spots, cream chest, black hooves. We will keep the ORIGINAL frames and interleave your NEW intermediate poses with them. Therefore do not redesign or simplify deer, do not change antler shape, torso length, head size, leg length, markings or shading style. Create ONLY 16 new full-body transparent sprites on a square 2048x2048 sheet arranged in FOUR columns and FOUR rows, with generous spacing and padding. Read left to right then top to bottom. No text, grid, background, water, floor, shadows or labels. All bodies face LEFT in side view; only the specified gaze frames turn the head. Keep consistent torso scale across all cells. OUTPUT ROWS 1-2: EIGHT actual HALF-WAY running poses to insert between the eight existing running poses in INPUT ROWS 3-4. Number the input run poses A-H left to right. Output run poses must be A/B midpoint, B/C midpoint, C/D midpoint, D/E midpoint, E/F midpoint, F/G midpoint, G/H midpoint, H/A midpoint. Slightly advance each leg's joint angles halfway toward its next pose, so these are NEW frames, not copies. Keep the spine, hips, neck and antlers aligned with the reference and avoid torso deformation. Include distinct stages of foreleg landing, front support, hindlegs coming forward, hind-leg push, suspension and foreleg reach. Exactly four anatomically connected legs, nearer limbs brighter and far limbs darker. OUTPUT ROW 3: FOUR progressive intermediate poses raising the head from the drinking pose of INPUT cell row1 col1 to the upright standing pose of INPUT row2 col1. Legs and torso remain PLANTED, rigid and unchanged; only neck/head/antlers articulate. First is head barely lifted from ground (20% raised), second muzzle knee-height (40%), third muzzle chest-height (60%), fourth head nearly upright (80%). Do not make these all head-down copies; show a clear gradual lift. OUTPUT ROW4: cell1 head angle HALF-WAY between INPUT row2 col1 (looking left) and row2 col2 (looking toward viewer); cell2 head angle HALF-WAY between INPUT row2 col2 and row2 col3 (looking backward over shoulder), with torso still facing left. Cell3 FIRST RUN START pose from standing: ears alert, head forward, torso slightly crouched, hind knees load, one front hoof begins lifting. Cell4 SECOND RUN START pose: pushes from hind hooves, torso leans forward to LEFT, front legs start extending, approaching INPUT run frame A. These final two poses bridge standing into running and must not depict an already full-speed stride. Maintain same relative pixel size and detail as input, no antialiasing blur, no motion blur, no double exposures, no blended silhouettes. Real alpha transparency.

HEAD AND START REFINEMENT — FINAL EIGHT FRAMES USED:
Create 8 intermediate animation sprites of EXACTLY this same adult pixel-art stag. Transparent 4-column by 2-row sprite sheet. This is a precision identity-preserving animation task, not a redesign. Reference 1 is drinking, Reference 2 is upright looking left, Reference 3 looking front, Reference 4 looking behind. Keep the original taller elegant neck, LONG tall branched antlers, high antler tines, and slender legs. Do not shorten the neck or antlers, do not make the torso rounder or squat. Keep SAME fur color, spots, black chunky pixel outlines and detail. In each equal cell 384x384 logical pixels (can upscale entire sheet), hooves baseline at y360, hips near x250, upper back near y185, body and legs in exact position seen in reference 2. A standing pose's antler tips reach y25. Leave full top space in all cells. ALL cells show one complete deer, same scale, no cropping. FIRST ROW: four gradual head-raising intermediates from reference1 to reference2: 1 muzzle just lifted off floor toward knee level, 2 muzzle at knee level, 3 muzzle at lower chest height, 4 muzzle at upper chest height but not yet standing fully upright. Head follows a smooth arc forward and upward. Keep body and legs fixed. SECOND ROW cell1: true halfway head turn from reference2 to reference3, i.e. head looking left-forward three-quarter toward viewer, torso remains left-facing. Cell2: true halfway turn from reference3 to reference4, head looking right-forward three-quarter, torso remains left-facing. Cell3: standing-to-run anticipation, body crouches slightly loading hind legs, long neck leans forward, one forehoof beginning to lift. Cell4: first push-off toward left, hind legs extend backward, front legs reach forward, body leans forward slightly, a small initial step instead of a big leap. Need smooth transitional poses that can be placed between the provided original frames. Full transparency real alpha. No labels, numbers, cells, shadows, backgrounds, white background, water, blur, antialiasing smoothing or blended double images. Crisp pixel art edges.

PACKAGING:
Eight running frames from the first sheet and all eight frames from the refinement sheet were used. The original 16 PNGs remain unchanged. New frames were extracted by connected alpha regions and placed on 384x384 canvases. The refinement frames were sized with nearest-neighbour sampling to match the established scale (0.85; 0.75 for the two start frames). Run intermediates were reordered to better match adjacent original leg silhouettes. The output is an approximation of inbetween animation; reference details are not pixel-identical in the newly generated frames.
